why: A found that the app's only user-facing path (OpenAIAgent.astream_chat) silently drops every tool call, so SEC Insights answers every financial question with its "Sorry, I...don't have an answer" fallback — diagnosed to the exact gate, reproduced with no Router in the path, fixed and tested on a branch — and is the only one of the two to ask whether a call should exist at all (the per-document agent that spends a whole LLM turn deciding to call a zero-argument function). B's migration and measurement hygiene are better, but it ranked a careful set of tune-ups against a product that currently returns nothing, and its probes drove SubQuestionQueryEngine directly rather than the real entry point, which is why it never saw the outage.
A_best: The astream_chat tool-loop bug: correct mechanism (role-only first chunk sets is_function_false_event before the tool call arrives), proven no-Router reproduction, before/after through the real handle_chat_message (1 request and an empty answer → 6 requests and a real figure), honest about the monkeypatch liability and sequenced into i7's FunctionAgent rework to delete it.
B_best: Discovering that the runtime's stack-derived spend label is useless for this app — 5 of 8 requests labelled with whatever module was on the stack, 2 unlabelled because the streaming agent runs on a worker thread — then fixing it with explicit per-workload headers so router.policy.json can actually target chat vs the RAG fan-out separately; plus the latency measurement that kills the obvious cost win (gpt-6-luna 17.5s vs gpt-4o-mini 5.5s on a full RAG turn).
A_worst: It left Router's spend/policy keying broken: it saw that call-stack labels resolve to an arbitrary FastAPI frame and responded by writing policy against defaults instead of fixing the labels, so no per-workload lever is reachable; and its headline cost item (gpt-6-luna, 64-72% cheaper on two prompts) never measured latency on a path it itself calls all-user-waiting, which B shows is a 3x regression. No treatment of the spend cap as a new single point of failure, and the outside check could not verify tools.py:156.
B_worst: It missed that the product doesn't work — every improvement is priced and sequenced against a chat feature that currently returns a canned apology — and its system judgment stops at the migration tune-up boundary: nothing questions whether any call should exist (no mention of the agent hop over a zero-argument polygon.io tool), the model decision ends in "no change yet", and prompt_cache_key is set to a constant feature label rather than the conversation id, which is the wrong granularity for the affinity it is buying.
